# Independent audit: concurrent cap-normal motion and global section cancellation


concurrent-cap-normal-motion-and-global-section-cancellation.md.
No mathematical correction is needed.

## 1. Coverage and the permitted parameter space

The common affine meeting-section form
u_i*(x-q(z))>=0 is sufficient for whole-space coverage under positive
spanning of the continuous normals. The minimum over unit directions
of max_i u_i*v is strictly positive, so the stated uniform perturbation
radius preserves this property. The argument includes points on the
meeting section because the halfspaces are closed.

The two-cap mixed counterexample correctly shows why merely retaining
one common ambient point does not suffice. Keeping the entire affine
meeting section changes the base coefficients consistently with the
continuous normals. Independent motions of several appearances of
a shared cap are expressly not licensed.

The finite positive-circuit certificate in Section 4 is exact:
the Neumann bound with epsilon||D^T||_infinity<1/3 makes
eta=(I-epsilon D)^(-T)1 positive, and its weighted sum of the
margins is identically zero. Invertibility leaves continuous rank d
and the unique positive dependence, so this proves an actual
positive circuit, not merely approximate coverage of the source.

## 2. Coarea differentiation for arbitrary proper convex sections

I checked the Fubini argument independently. At a proper cut, the
relative interior of the section lies in the interior of the full
convex fiber. Otherwise a supporting hyperplane at such a relative
interior point would have to contain the section plane and make
that plane supporting, contradicting properness. The boundary of
this full-dimensional section in its own plane has zero
(d-1)-measure.

On almost every transverse line the signed swept interval therefore
has the asserted derivative. Its absolute length divided by the
parameter is uniformly bounded on the bounded projection of the
fiber, because the denominator stays at least |u|/2. Dominated
convergence yields precisely

    derivative = v*sum_z integral (x-q(z)) d tau_z,

with the coarea factor 1/|u|. The sign is positive for an outward
gain of the captured set. The residual is orthogonal to u, so
choosing v=-R gives derivative -|R|^2 and is tangent to the normal
sphere to first order. The statement excludes supporting-facet
degeneracies explicitly; it does not substitute an arbitrary trace
coefficient at those fibers. Strict full/empty fibers stay fixed.
The d=1 proper-cut interpretation is consistent.

## 3. Lone-simplex motions

The section-centroid coordinates and
delta_i*a=-||delta_i||^2 are correct. Integrating the explicit
barycentric margin perturbation gives -S_i||delta_i||^2, with
S_i=dV(1-a_i)^(d-1). The distinction between the chosen barycentric
norm and physical Euclidean distance on a general simplex is retained.

At a noncanonical concurrent point at most one index has zero
section-centroid displacement. The one-high formulas in (9) are
exact. Its high cap really is an ordinary minimizing cap: the
vertex-centered inner homothetic simplex of scale 1/3 has centroid
at the meeting point, and its Grunbaum cap is exactly that outer
high cap. Thus a claim of strictly improving every cap by fixed-point
normal rotation alone would be false, as the note states.

Adding the prescribed common meeting-point motion corrects precisely
that stationary index. In both cases of Section 4,
h_i+k_i||delta_i||^2=1 for every i and sum h_i=0. All first cap
derivatives are therefore -S_i<0. Positive spanning and proper-cut
smoothness give one common positive interval of actual strictly
decreasing cap masses. The canonical obstruction and d=1 exception
are also correctly separated.

## 4. Actual global star and minimality

All endpoint and middle cuts in the star are proper. Reflection
identifies the endpoint section coarea measures and reverses
their section displacements. The middle section is symmetric.
Both the continuous section first moment and the base first
moment therefore vanish exactly. This proves stationarity for
arbitrary infinitesimal ambient cap-normal motions through the
central point, while retaining every actual source fiber.

The stronger exact mass-flatness follows from symmetry of the
entire mixed measure and null boundary for every nonvertical
through-origin hyperplane. It is not merely a first-order inference.
The explicit common-section motions preserve cover; arbitrary
through-point motions retain this mass statement without an
unsupported coverage claim.

A single retained circuit is inclusion-minimal: sufficiently small
positive multiples of its centered simplex vertices, at base zero,
lie inside the actual middle body and are covered by their respective
cap alone. The note correctly distinguishes this fact and the exact
global force cancellation from the multigroup physical variance
stress, which is not retained after deleting groups.
The binary isolation qualification is valid by finite strict
exclusion margins.

## 5. Verification

The standard-library verifier
supporting computation verify_concurrent_normal_motion_and_section_cancellation.py was
rerun and passes 29 noncanonical groups and 441 exact finite
strict-decrease paths, positive-circuit solves, the canonical
exception, the mixed cover guard, and the reflected moment checks.
The arbitrary convex-fiber differentiability and all-parameter
coverage claims follow from the proof, not from those finite tests.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
